record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; the referenced status documents, paper sections, and result files were not read. The README says the paper write-up is still in progress.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports ablation results that challenge the effectiveness of the standard rank-1 mean-difference recipe on Gemma 4, and reports that the cleanest tested rank-1 variant leaves substantial refusal in place.
record.gate_note: Rows below use only outcomes explicitly reported in the README. It mentions a random-direction control in the sweep but does not state that control's result separately. Commands, planned analyses, and results only referred to in other files are not treated as reported outcomes.
record.test_reason: The authors build difference-in-means refusal directions on Gemma 4 E4B-it, apply rank-1 weight-edit ablation, and report should_refuse rates. The standard recipe leaves refusal at 100%, and a modified direction cuts it only to 40.5%. They argue refusal on Gemma 4 is not cleanly rank-1. This bears on V1, V2 (self-made weight edits) and V4. Evidence is README summaries only.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find the activation refusal direction effectively rank-1. The standard rank-1 recipe fails on Gemma 4 E4B (100% refusal at int8 and bf16). Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization against the harmless mean is the load-bearing step, giving a 60% relative reduction. The residual refusal on extreme topics, together with OBLITERATUS's multi-rank edits, suggests full removal is not rank-1.
record.recipe_differences: The project reports using an Mlabonne/Arditi-style rank-1 weight perturbation on selected projection weights, plus a modified D3 direction recipe; it does not report the original all-layer, all-position residual-stream projection procedure. This is a course research project, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says standard rank-1 results differ from the D3 recipe, which uses chat-template-applied activations, per-layer winsorization at 99.5%, and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization against the harmless mean. It also reports tests at int8 and bf16.

fits_no_version.finding: Published uncensored edits of Gemma 4 differ in rank (OBLITERATUS median rank_95=6; TrevorJS rank-1). Their edited subspaces are nearly orthogonal (|cos| 0.08), and neither top singular vector aligns with the activation refusal direction (|cos| ≈0.04).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different released abliteration methods modify different weight subspaces, not aligned with the activation-derived refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-category over-refusal directions (medical, survival, etc.) cluster at +0.93 cosine with each other. They are orthogonal to the should_refuse direction (mean cos −0.015).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-refusal directions for benign-but-flagged categories are separate from the harmful-refusal direction.

record.problems: Evidence is presented only as README headline summaries; the README does not provide prompt-level counts or uncertainty estimates for the ablation outcomes. It does not report general-capability measurements, and the referenced detailed results and paper are not included in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported outcomes were available in the README for the random-direction control, released TrevorJS or HauhauCS behavioral evaluations, or the referenced weight-diff and selective-safety result files. The README mentions these materials but does not give their corresponding outcomes in sufficient detail.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; capability retention (no capability check); all-layer, all-position activation ablation.
Refusal rates of released abliterated models (OBLITERATUS, TrevorJS, HauhauCS). Results files exist but no numbers appear in the README.
Affine or cone models of refusal; multi-rank or multi-direction ablation, which the authors list as future work.

missing.what: Base Gemma 4 E4B should_refuse baseline (100%; E2B 95.2%) and emergency_medical refusal (2%; E2B 12%)
Result of the random-direction control in the M2c sweep, and the per-stage M6 cascade results showing that variants without Gram-Schmidt have no effect
Behavioural refusal rates for the released HauhauCS, OBLITERATUS and TrevorJS models
Norm-preserving biprojection adds no effect over vanilla projection; row-norm change is 0.03–0.07%

record.verdict_notes: Course project with an unfinished paper. Evidence comes from README headlines only: no uncertainty, n=42 for the key result, no capability checks. The intervention is a weight edit on selected projections, not the original all-layer projection. The failure of the standard recipe may reflect implementation or direction-construction choices, which the authors themselves show matter.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, effects on general capabilities, or a direct test of projection at every layer and position.
The README does not give separate behavioral results for each released abliteration variant.
The README does not test affine or cone models of refusal geometry.
